name: Coastal Lava Cliff Walk
reason: Wikivoyage Upolu names it only inside the O Le Pupu-Pu'e park line; no second counted source or route detail found; a walk inside a park that is likely its own destination. Case for: named trail. Against: part of a larger spot.

name: Papapapai-tai Falls
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Upolu (100 m drop, 2 km south of Lanoto'o turn-off) and Lonely Planet (lookout about 14 km south of Apia over a 100 m fall). Second-tier waterfall a guide singles out. Against: roadside lookout, short visit.

name: Aleipata Islands
reason: Lonely Planet's top-place is 'Aleipata Beaches & Reefs' (covered by Lalomanu Beach and Namu'a); the islands themselves only appear in tour listings. Against: near-duplicate of Lalomanu/Namu'a, boat-only.

name: Apolima
reason: Only Wikipedia and blogs/tour sites found; Wikivoyage Upolu does not list it; access by local boat, partly by invitation. No counted source resolved (not evidence against).

name: Samoa Cultural Village
reason: Lonely Planet 'Top Choice' and top-places list: weekday cultural sessions (weaving, siapo, tatau, kava, umu lunch) behind the Tourism Authority fale; Afar and Trip.com confirm Mon-Fri 9-17, free with donation. Permanent venue. Against: weekdays only, second source is aggregator.

name: Mulinu'u Peninsula
reason: Wikivoyage Apia lists it (parliament, observatory, tombs) but LP's 'Cape Mulinu'u' top place is the Savai'i headland, not this peninsula. Mostly exteriors and tombs. Case for: guide-listed area. Against: civic exteriors.

name: Apia Fresh Produce Market
reason: Marketi Fou trades Mon-Sat (daily hall rule OK), kava by the cup, local food; only Wikivoyage Apia counted. Marginal: one source.

name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral, Apia
reason: Wikivoyage Apia See #7 singles out its cupolas and ornaments as setting it apart, rebuilt and reopened 2014; a landmark a guide names, enterable. Against: single source, church.

name: Sopo'aga Waterfalls
reason: Lonely Planet lists Sopo'aga Falls (54 m into a gorge by the south coast road), tours routinely stop; viewpoint through a garden, small fee, about 15 minute visit. Counted source exists, so not OSM-only. Against: roadside, short.

name: Fuipisia Waterfalls
reason: Twin 54 m falls near Apia named by waterfall guides and blogs and apparently LP (poi ids appeared in search, page unreadable). Counted source UNRESOLVED; short walk, village fee.

name: Fagaloa Bay
reason: Bay is the setting; the draw is the Uafato Conservation Area (see conservation zone entry). Near-duplicate.

name: Fagaloa Bay – Uafato Tiavea Conservation Zone
reason: Lonely Planet lists Uafato Conservation Area: 14 sq km rainforest to ocean, carvers demonstrate, rough road round Fagaloa Bay; village bird-watching trail opened. Samoa's UNESCO tentative list. Against: remote, rough road, one counted source; name it Uafato Conservation Area.

name: Uafato Bay
reason: Same place as the Uafato Conservation Area entry; duplicate.

name: Falefa Valley
reason: Appears only as a photo caption on Wikivoyage Samoa; the visitor stop is Falefa Falls, not a valley.

name: Falemauga Caves
reason: Wikipedia and archaeology news only; sources say only experienced potholers should enter (dangerous); no visitor route.

name: Sinalei Beach
reason: Beach of a private resort (Sinalei Reef Resort, no children under 12); no visitor source names the beach.

name: Lotofaga Beach
reason: Lotofaga is the village of To Sua; no visitor source names a beach there (To Sua is kept).

name: Saleapaga Beach
reason: Only a beach-fale lodging line (FaoFao) on Wikivoyage; no source names the beach as a stop.

name: Maninoa Beach
reason: Only the Coconuts resort line on Wikivoyage; resort beach, no visitor source.

name: Vailima Botanical Gardens
reason: Only tour-operator and Expedia listings, 13-acre government garden; no counted source found (LP unresolved). Wikivoyage Apia does not list it.

name: Mulifanua
reason: Ferry port for Savai'i; Wikivoyage Samoa mentions only an archaeological site with nothing to see.

name: Mount Fito
reason: Wikivoyage Upolu names it only as the park's highest peak; no source gives a visitor route. Part of O Le Pupu-Pu'e.

name: Peapea Cave
reason: Wikivoyage and Lonely Planet both name it: lava tube with swiftlets, 10 min walk from the road, locked, guide needed, guided look about 10 minutes. Two counted sources but a very short visit.

name: Paia Dwarfs Cave
reason: Wikivoyage Savaii See #2 and Lonely Planet 'Dwarf's Cave' (lava tube, guide leads; bring torch). Two counted sources, a real guided activity.

name: Mount Matavanu Lava Fields
reason: Wikivoyage Savaii See #4 and Lonely Planet 'Mt Matavanu Crater' both list it; 3 h walk to the 1905-11 lava field and crater. A distinct hike.

name: Sapapaliʻi
reason: Wikivoyage only: a monument to John Williams's 1830 landing, a minor memorial with nothing else named (rule 3). Not found in LP.

name: Tafua Peninsula Rainforest Preserve
reason: Wikivoyage Savaii See #10 and Lonely Planet (superb rainforest, rugged lava coast with cliffs and sea arches) both name it; walk to the crater.

name: Falealupo Church Ruins
reason: Lonely Planet's Savai'i text covers the cyclone-destroyed Falealupo village and collapsed lava tube; church ruins named only by blogs. Counted source for the ruins themselves unresolved.

name: Aganoa Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Do names it only as the surf operator's base; no sight or visit described, and no second source found.

name: Manase
reason: Wikivoyage Do lists north-coast surf at Manase; beach-fale village with a beach; no counted source describes a stop. Marginal.

name: Wreck of the Juno
reason: Wikivoyage Do names the 1881 wreck as a popular dive (about 22 m, 5 min boat) but only the sole operator Dive Savaii (listed temporarily closed) reaches it. Case for: named dive site. Against: dive-operator access, one counted source.

name: Satuiatua
reason: Wikivoyage lists only the resort; Wikipedia and blogs call the beach picturesque; no counted visitor source found.

name: Salelologa
reason: Ferry town and bus hub with the main produce market (guides advise stocking up); a gateway at low rank rather than an attraction.

name: Faleālupo Beach
reason: Only a Sleep line on Wikivoyage ('one of the best beaches'); no stand-alone counted entry. Against: lodging mention.

name: Falealupo
reason: Keep as wrapper reject: the peninsula's draws are separate (Falealupo Rainforest Preserve kept, Cape Mulinu'u, church ruins). Lonely Planet's top-places list has 'Cape Mulinu'u' (Savai'i's westernmost point, spirit-path site) which is NOT among the candidates and should be added as a keep.

name: Fagamalo
reason: Village known as surf and dive base; no sight (dive base of the sole operator).

name: Lano
reason: No visitor source found for Lano.

name: Central Savaiʻi Rainforest
reason: No visitor infrastructure or source found; the walkable parts are Matavanu and the preserves.

name: Moso's Footprint
reason: No counted visitor source found (UNRESOLVED, only Wikipedia); small roadside feature.

name: Silisili
reason: Highest peak, no visitor route in any source read.
